evidence.text: Implemented and locally verified evaluate(): it checks sorted missing required request conditions first; filters records by claim, non-withdrawn state, verification policy, and canonical-JSON equality for every required condition; applies supersession only among eligible records; reports no-match, conflict, supported, or Boolean-false unsupported with sorted source IDs; does not mutate inputs. Current report evaluates vertical_rate as supported 30 from S1 and device_validated as unsupported false from D1.

Verified boundary behavior with actual local assertions: missing required names are sorted; absent calibration is unknown rather than zero; zero is supported; require_verified excludes unverified records; withdrawn records are excluded; an ineligible superseder cannot remove an eligible source; supersession among eligible records removes the old source; canonical object key order agrees; disagreements remain conflicts even with a majority; only Boolean false is unsupported; inputs remain unchanged.

Unresolved limits: the contract does not define malformed/non-JSON Python inputs, mixed-type or missing source IDs, duplicate source IDs, duplicate required-condition names, or non-finite numeric values. Implementation is verified for ordinary JSON data with string source IDs and unique required-condition names. Canonical comparison uses sorted compact JSON serialization; required-condition matching ignores non-required condition fields.

Milestone complete: work.py implements evaluate and report.json matches both current requests. Current-data check, independent boundary assertions, immutability assertions, and Python compilation all passed.
